anomalies.observed: The two otherwise-identical CAN interface connectors do not share a pin-1 net. 'CAN Interface A' (J10) pin 1 is on net NET0146, while 'CAN Interface B' (J29) pin 1 is on net NET0202. NET0202 is the 3.3 V VDD rail used by the CAN/serial controllers (it feeds U47/U21/U44/U11 VDD and is decoupled by C6/C35/C36/C86), so J29 pin 1 is tied directly to a supply rail.
anomalies.expected: J10 and J29 are the same connector type carrying the same CAN/control signals on pins 2-7, so pin 1 should carry the same shared control/e-stop net on both, not a 3.3 V supply rail.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS area: J10 'CAN Interface A' pin1 = NET0146, J29 'CAN Interface B' pin1 = NET0202; pins 2-7 of both = NET0211 / NET0193 / NET0068 / NET0195 / 5V_switched_CAN / NET0001
feeding an ESTOP_OUT signal shared with the CAN connectors J2/J13

anomalies.impact: CAN B connector pin 1 is connected to the 3.3 V rail instead of the shared control/e-stop net, so that connector does not carry the e-stop signal on pin 1 and instead exposes the 3.3 V supply on the connector.

parsed.summary: The two CAN interface connectors J10 and J29 are otherwise identical but disagree on pin 1: J10 pin 1 is on the e-stop/control net NET0146 while J29 pin 1 is tied to the 3.3 V VDD net NET0202, which would put a supply rail on a connector signal pin and break the shared e-stop/control signal; this is the only clear deviation found, at low confidence.
